description: Saved analyses whose stages contain a displacement or rewrite that Replay does not recognize as movement. Each claim's moment now introduces the occurrences it relates to an earlier occurrence of the same object, with the new parents that attach them; the earlier occurrence keeps its form until then, and all other construction keeps its own steps. Frames are the 1-based Replay frames on origin/main 5c00a19.

cases.description: Stage 3 raises 我 to Spec-TP with a claim whose name and fields are Chinese (主语内部合并: 低位, 目标头, 高位), so Replay does not recognize it as movement. The new occurrence rSubjectHigh shares lineage with rSubjectBase, which the claim also anchors; lineage continuity showed it as a separate root from the stage's first step (Select T, frame 21), and an ordinary merge attached it. The claim's moment now introduces rSubjectHigh with the new TP that attaches it above T′, and silences rSubjectBase, which keeps its word until then.

cases.sentence: 我昨天看见的那个人走了。

derivationStages.stageRecord: 选择词汇动词“看见”，将它与无声的名词性关系算子外部合并，形成由动词投射标签的句法对象。算子在此首次出现，获得被看见者的题元角色；它尚未移位。“看见”作为一个词汇动词处理，不另行假设“看”和“见”之间的句法移位。所有投射均是合并所得对象的标签，而非预先提供的短语结构模板。
derivationStages.statement: 建立关系从句中“看见”的宾语位置。

derivationStages.stageRecord: 先将无声的及物轻动词与动词短语合并，再外部合并“我”，使其成为“看见”的感知者。随后将已经处于宾语位置的关系算子内部合并到轻动词短语边缘，为跨越该阶段的后续关系化提供出口；宾语位置保留无声副本。最后把“昨天”附加到扩展的轻动词短语，限定看见事件的时间，而不限定尚未建立的主句离开事件。
derivationStages.statement: 引入关系从句的感知者、算子边缘位置和时间修饰语。

derivationStages.stageRecord: 将无声的从属时态头与已有结构合并，再把已经在轻动词短语内出现的“我”内部合并到时态域主语位置。高位副本发音，低位副本不发音，因此“我”在线性次序上位于“昨天”之前。这里的时态头组织从属小句，不给汉语动词添加形态时态；“昨天”提供显性的时间定位。
derivationStages.statement: 建立关系从句的主语位置，得到“我昨天看见”的次序。

values.类型: 带宾语空位的限制性关系从句

derivationStages.stageRecord: 将位于从属时态域右侧的关系补语标记“的”与该时态域合并，建立关系从句类型。随后把已经处于轻动词短语边缘的算子内部合并到补语域边缘，形成依次连接宾语位置、轻动词边缘和关系从句边缘的链。算子各位置均无声，所以可听见的部分是“我昨天看见的”。此处采用外部中心语分析：后面的“人”不从从句宾语位置提升出来。
derivationStages.statement: 用句末“的”和算子移位完成宾语关系从句。

values.解释: 所指的人是我昨天看见的对象

values.体解释: 离开事件作为已实现的完整事件呈现

derivationStages.stageRecord: 先以“人”为名词核心，依次合并分类词“个”和指示限定词“那”；“个”提供个体计数单位，“那”确定指示性的名词域。再将已完成的关系从句附加到整个指示名词域左侧，得到“我昨天看见的那个人”。这种高附加保留输入中关系从句先于“那个人”的次序，关系算子与“人”的限制域建立解释联系。随后建立不及物的“走”及其轻动词域，把完整名词短语外部合并为离开者。本分析把“走”作为可带外部行动者的离开谓词，不另设无声宾语。最后合并右置的完成体头“了”，使完成体作用于离开事件；此时尚未发生主句主语移位。
derivationStages.statement: 建立完整主语及带完成体的主句谓词。

values.链表示: 高位完整名词短语与低位语迹

derivationStages.stageRecord: 合并无声的主句时态头，再将上一阶段已位于主句轻动词域内的完整名词短语内部合并到时态域主语位置。主句这条移位链采用语迹记法：原位置保留无声的名词性语迹，高位出现保留原名词短语的全部词汇结构。因此关系从句及“那个人”只发音一次。该时态头不带显性时态形态，主句的事件时间也不必等同于关系从句的“昨天”。完成体头不参与主语移位，也不要求另设动词移位。
derivationStages.statement: 将完整关系名词短语提升到主句主语位置。

values.读法: 那位我昨天看见的人已经离开

derivationStages.stageRecord: 将无声的陈述补语头与主句时态域合并，建立完整的根句。该读法断言被关系从句限定的那个人发生了离开事件；句末位置的“了”来自较低的完成体域，不另加入句末变化状态助词。树的发音次序为“我昨天看见的那个人走了”，与输入完全对应。
derivationStages.statement: 完成“了”为完成体标记的陈述句分析。

cases.description: Stage 9 moves the complex head mTHead to C. The claim names its contained heads in lists, so movement recovery stops at MOVEMENT_ENDPOINTS_UNRESOLVED and the claim is neutral. The new complex mTHeadAtC appeared whole at the unrelated Select C step (frame 49). The claim's moment now introduces it with the new C head complex and the CP that attaches it above TP.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run, commit 53a7c7f, 18 October 2026 (indexed-token night batch, 27-sv-embedded-negation, analysis 1 of 1).
cases.sentence: Jag vet att han inte kom.

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge combines the lexically inflected verb kom with the pronominal DP han. Kom is analyzed as an unaccusative arrival predicate, so han originates as its internal Theme rather than as an external argument. The past-tense form is present lexically; its finite licensing will be established when embedded T is introduced. Projection labels such as VP and DP abbreviate labels inherited from the projecting head in Bare Phrase Structure, rather than presupposing an X-bar template.
derivationStages.statement: Build the embedded arrival predicate with its internal argument.

values.realization: lexically inflected kom; no overt raising across negation

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent, non-external-argument-introducing v combines with the arrival VP. Neg inte then combines above vP, establishing negation over the arrival predicate. Silent finite T merges above NegP and agrees with the accessible DP han, licensing nominative Case and valuing its own person-number features as third-person singular. T also licenses the past-tense form kom. This analysis treats kom as lexically inflected and licensed by a dependency with T, not as the result of overt V-to-T movement or a separately pronounced tense affix. Consequently, kom remains below inte, as required by this Swedish embedded clause.
derivationStages.statement: Establish embedded negation and finite T without raising kom across inte.

values.pronunciation: higher occurrence pronounced; lower occurrence silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge copies han from the VP-internal position shown previously to the edge of TP, satisfying embedded T's subject requirement. The higher DP is pronounced, while the lower occurrence and its terminal are silent. External Merge then adds att, which types the result as a finite declarative complement. Att is a complementizer, not an infinitival marker here: it selects the finite TP containing han and past-tense kom. This embedded C does not trigger the matrix V2 movement pattern, leaving the pronounced order att han inte kom.
derivationStages.statement: Raise han to embedded subject position and close the clause with att.

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge combines vet with the completed att-clause. Vet selects a propositional CP complement, yielding the interpretation that the matrix subject knows the proposition that he did not come. The CP is an argument of vet, not an adjunct or an infinitival clause. The matrix pronoun Jag is also introduced as a separate DP, available for subsequent external Merge. Vet is introduced in its lexical present-tense form; later finite licensing and head movement preserve that whole-word realization.
derivationStages.statement: Select the finite clause as the complement of vet.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Silent matrix v first combines with the VP headed by vet. Jag then externally merges at the edge of that v-domain. Together, v and the selected knowledge predicate license Jag as the experiencer or holder of the knowledge state. This is the matrix subject's first-merge position; it has not yet moved to a finite subject position or to the matrix clause edge.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce the matrix experiencer in the v-domain.

values.pronunciation: higher V occurrence pronounced; lower V occurrence silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: The occurrence of vet in V, already present in the preceding workspace, undergoes head movement to v. The resulting complex v head contains a higher V occurrence followed by silent v. The higher occurrence of vet is pronounced and the original V occurrence is silent. This local step provides the verbal head that will subsequently raise through T to matrix C; the clausal complement remains in its original VP position.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the matrix lexical verb to v.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Silent finite T externally merges above the matrix vP. It agrees with Jag, licensing nominative Case and valuing T's person-number features as first-person singular. T also licenses the lexical present-tense form vet in the complex v head. Agreement is represented independently of overt agreement morphology: Swedish vet does not change form for the subject's person or number. T's subject-edge requirement and its attraction of the verbal head remain to be satisfied by movement from the positions now visible.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce matrix finite T and establish its licensing dependencies.

values.dependency: local movement of the complex verbal head to finite T
values.pronunciation: vet pronounced in the higher complex; lower complex silent
TP-edge occurrence pronounced; vP occurrence silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: The complex v head raises from its previously established position to T, carrying vet with it and leaving a silent lower complex. The pronounced V occurrence is now inside the complex T head. Jag then undergoes Internal Merge from the vP edge to the TP edge, satisfying T's subject requirement; the vP occurrence becomes silent. Head movement and subject movement affect different objects, and neither requires an intermediate position created by the other. Their stated order determines the presentation here. The result is a finite matrix TP whose subject and verbal head are both available for the subsequent V2 step.
derivationStages.statement: Move the verbal complex to T and Jag to the TP edge.

relations.relation: matrix clause typing and V2 requirements

requirements: one phrase at the CP edge

values.pronunciation: vet pronounced in C; lower T complex silent
CP-edge occurrence pronounced; TP-edge occurrence silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent declarative matrix C merges with the completed TP. Unlike embedded att, this C attracts the finite verbal head and requires a phrase at its left edge. First, the complex T head raises from the T position shown in the preceding stage to C, carrying the v and V occurrences with it; the entire lower T complex becomes silent. Next, Jag moves from the previously established TP edge to the CP edge, and that intermediate subject occurrence becomes silent. These operations satisfy the matrix C requirements and yield the subject-initial V2 order Jag vet. The embedded complement remains att han inte kom: han is pronounced at its TP edge, inte precedes the unmoved embedded lexical verb, and kom retains past tense. Only the highest matrix subject and verbal occurrences are pronounced. The terminal yield is exactly the six supplied tokens; the quotation punctuation is not an additional input token.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the matrix V2 clause and derive Jag vet att han inte kom.

cases.description: Stages 4 and 8 pied-pipe the PP. Both claims name a landing and a contained operator, so recovery finds two landings and the claims are neutral. In stage 4 the new copy pp1 appeared at the ordinary merge of vEdge (frame 29); in stage 8 pp2 was projected over 'to' at its own Project step (frame 43). Each claim's moment now introduces its copy with the new parent that attaches it. In stage 8 the recognized operator-variable claim still owns wh2 and introduces it at its own later moment, as diagnosed by RELATION_TIMING_CONFLICT.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character spell-out contract (v1), commit 53a7c7f, 18 October 2026 (spell-out night batch, 11-en-relative-pied-piping, analysis 1 of 1).
cases.sentence: This is the man to whom I gave the book.

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge combines the determiner the with book and the preposition to with the relative pronoun whom. The resulting objects are a definite DP and a PP. The preposition licenses oblique case on whom. Whom supplies the relative-operator feature that will eventually license displacement of the containing PP. Labels identify the projecting heads; no additional unary projections or intermediate bar levels are assumed.
derivationStages.statement: Build the theme DP and the relative operator PP.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Gave first merges with the book, establishing the theme relation. The resulting verbal object then merges with to whom, establishing the selected goal relation. Both merged objects project the verbal head. This binary, layered structure treats the PP as an internal argument rather than an optional modifier and gives the unmoved order gave the book to whom. Gave is retained as one lexical terminal; its past-tense form will be licensed by the relative clause's finite T.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the internal argument domain of gave.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent transitive v merges with the verbal domain, and I externally merges as its subject. The external argument receives the agent role. Transitive v licenses accusative case on the book. The subject remains in its first-merged position, and the goal PP remains inside the verbal domain.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce the giver and the transitive phase head.

values.pronunciation: edge copy pronounced; argument copy silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: The edge feature of transitive v permits Internal Merge of to whom above the external argument. This intermediate position makes the PP accessible to the later relative C. Pied-piping carries to together with whom; the analysis does not extract whom alone or strand the preposition. The original PP occurrence is retained as a silent copy, while the edge occurrence is currently pronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Move the entire goal PP to the transitive phase edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Silent past T merges with the edged vP. T agrees with I and licenses its nominative case; the intervening PP is not an eligible nominative goal. Past T licenses the lexical past form gave without requiring overt lexical-verb movement to T. This analysis therefore keeps gave in the verbal domain and represents no separate pronounced tense morpheme.
derivationStages.statement: Establish finite tense and subject agreement in the relative clause.

values.pronunciation: TP copy pronounced; agent copy silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: The subject-position requirement of finite T triggers Internal Merge of I at the TP edge. The earlier agent occurrence remains in vP as a silent copy. The PP at the vP edge remains available for subsequent relative movement; subject movement neither reassigns its case nor changes its argument relation.
derivationStages.statement: Raise I to the relative clause's subject position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent relative C selects the finite TP. Its relative feature requires an operator at the CP edge. The accessible operator is whom inside the PP already at the vP edge. C is silent in this pied-piped relative construction; no pronounced that is introduced.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce the silent relative complementizer.

values.pronunciation: CP copy pronounced; intermediate copy silent

values.interpretation: abstraction over the recipient of the giving event

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge moves the whole PP from its previously established vP-edge position to the relative CP edge. The new highest occurrence supplies to whom, and the intermediate occurrence becomes silent. The highest whom functions as the relative operator binding the goal variable interpreted at the original argument occurrence. The retained lower copies preserve the preposition's case relation and the verb's goal relation.
derivationStages.statement: Complete relative pied-piping to the CP edge.

values.interpretation: man who is the recipient of the book
contextually identifiable man satisfying the relative restriction

derivationStages.stageRecord: The completed relative CP externally merges as a postnominal restrictor of man. The nominal head supplies the label of the combined nominal object, and the determiner the then merges above it. The external noun is interpreted as the antecedent of the relative operator, not as a displaced occurrence from inside the relative clause. Thus the analysis commits to an externally headed restrictive relative rather than noun raising. The determiner takes scope over the nominal restriction as a whole.
derivationStages.statement: Form the definite nominal containing the restrictive relative.

values.interpretation: the demonstrative referent is the man described by the definite nominal

derivationStages.stageRecord: The copular verb is merges with the definite nominal complement, and the demonstrative This merges as the subject of the resulting copular predicate. This is a complete demonstrative DP, not a determiner taking an unpronounced noun. The copula identifies its referent with the man described by the complement. The copular domain is analyzed without an agentive v layer: its subject is first merged within VP and the copula can subsequently raise directly to T.
derivationStages.statement: Build the matrix copular predication.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Silent present T merges above the copular VP. T agrees with the closest subject, This, valuing third-person singular agreement and licensing nominative case. These features license the selected copular form is. T is established as a separate head before copular movement, so the next operation has an independently represented landing site.
derivationStages.statement: Establish present tense and matrix subject agreement.

values.pronunciation: higher copular occurrence pronounced; lower occurrence silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: The copula moves from its previously represented V position to T, forming a complex head labeled by T. The lower verbal occurrence becomes silent, while the higher occurrence retains the lexical form is. With no intervening v head in this nonagentive copular structure, the movement is local. The abstract T remains silent within the complex head; is remains a single pronounced terminal rather than being split into separate written-word realizations.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the copula to matrix T.

values.pronunciation: TP copy pronounced; VP copy silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix T's subject-position requirement triggers Internal Merge of This from its VP position to the TP edge. The lower occurrence becomes silent. The pronounced matrix order is now This is followed by the complete definite nominal, including its relative clause.
derivationStages.statement: Raise This to the matrix subject position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent declarative C merges with the matrix TP and closes the root clause. No matrix operator movement or subject–auxiliary inversion is required. The completed tree pronounces This is the man to whom I gave the book: only the highest subject and relative-PP copies and the raised copular occurrence are pronounced. The relative remains inside the nominal complement, and its goal dependency terminates in the silent PP argument of gave.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the declarative sentence.

cases.description: Stage 3 fronts the object wh-phrase. The neutral rewrite owned only the trace left in the object position, not the new copy frontedObject, which therefore appeared only at the Stage Record (frame 35). The claim relates frontedObject to the preceding occurrence object, so its moment now introduces the copy with the trace.
cases.source: GPT-6 Astra, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run, commit ee11d20, 18 October 2026 (second bug-hunt batch, 26-bg-multiple-wh, analysis 1 of 1).

derivationStages.stageRecord: The Bulgarian sentence is an interrogative perfect clause meaning 'Who has bought what?'. In this Government and Binding analysis, the subject is generated in Spec-IP, without a separate VP-internal subject position. The participle купил heads V′ and takes the interrogative pronominal DP какво as its complement. The predicate assigns its external Agent role to the subject DP Кой and its internal Theme role to какво. Finite I, realized as е, licenses nominative Case on Кой; V governs its complement and assigns accusative Case to какво. This is the standard-language subject–object analysis: Кой is the nominative personal interrogative, whereas an accusative personal interrogative would normally be кого. The finite auxiliary selects the participial VP and establishes the perfect construction; е is third-person singular, and купил has masculine singular participial agreement with the subject. A silent interrogative C heads CP and takes IP as its complement. The two interrogative DPs are still in their argument positions, so their surface indices identify lexical tokens but do not yet represent their final order. The auxiliary is generated in I; neither auxiliary inversion nor participial movement is assumed.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the underlying argument structure and finite perfect clause before wh-fronting.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The subject DP moves from the previously represented Spec-IP position to Spec-CP, leaving an unpronounced DP trace. Its pronounced occurrence now occupies a nonargument position, while the trace retains the chain's Agent position and nominative licensing. Moving the structurally higher wh-argument first implements the superiority requirement for the neutral Bulgarian multiple-wh order. The object remains in its V-complement position at this intermediate stage; its later fronting therefore cannot be mistaken for movement from an already fronted position. The subject landing site enters the wh-licensing configuration with interrogative C. The subject trace is antecedent-governed by the Spec-CP occurrence in this local dependency; the null C introduces no overt-complementizer intervention. This analysis uses traces rather than unpronounced lexical copies.
derivationStages.statement: Front the higher wh-argument to Spec-CP and establish the subject A′-chain.

values.landingPosition: left adjunct to C′ below Spec-CP

values.configuration: additional wh-phrase in the interrogative C-domain

values.interpretation: which person x and which thing y are such that x has bought y

derivationStages.stageRecord: The object DP now moves from the V-complement position shown in the preceding workspace and leaves a silent trace there. Its landing site is left-adjoined to C′, below the subject in Spec-CP. This recursive C′ adjunction is the selected X-bar implementation of Bulgarian CP-level multiple-wh fronting: it creates a single interrogative left periphery containing both wh-phrases, not two clauses. The subject remains higher than the object, producing Кой какво rather than reversing their order. The object chain preserves the Theme role and accusative Case established at its argument position. The fronted object is licensed in the same interrogative C-domain as the subject, and its trace is lexically governed by купил, satisfying the Empty Category Principle for the object trace. Both fronted DPs A′-bind their respective traces, providing two variables under one interrogative operator domain; pair-list and contextually single-pair answers do not require different syntactic structures here. The unchanged auxiliary е remains in I, after the completed wh-cluster and before the participle. Thus the pronounced terminals are exactly Кой какво е купил. The question mark is orthographic punctuation and is not a supplied input token.
derivationStages.statement: Front the object below the subject within CP and complete the multiple-wh question.

cases.description: Stage 2 merges one shared object in both verb phrases: the claim relates the new occurrence object-sell to the preceding object-buy. The rewrite owned only object-buy, so its moment showed object-sell without its words (frame 20) and vp-sell and object-sell's words appeared only at the Stage Record (frame 21). vp-buy is now an ordinary merge, and the claim's moment introduces the complete object-sell with vp-sell.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run, commit ee11d20, 18 October 2026 (second bug-hunt batch, 07-en-rnr, analysis 1 of 1).
cases.sentence: Mary bought, and John sold, the house.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The comma-delimited final phrase supports a right-node-raising analysis: the house is the object of both bought and sold, but is pronounced only once, after the coordinated clauses. The derivation adopts copy-based, across-the-board rightward movement, rather than inserting an independently interpreted missing object after bought. The object DP is initially a separate syntactic object; its surface pronunciation is not assigned yet. Mary and John are proper-name DPs. Projection labels such as DP and VP describe the labels of recursively merged objects, not a pre-existing X-bar template. Punctuation guides the constructional analysis but supplies no syntactic terminal.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the lexical objects for a shared-object coordination.

relations.relation: parallel Merge and internal theta-role assignment

values.identity: The two complement occurrences belong to one shared DP.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Bought merges with the available DP, establishing its theme argument. Sold then merges with another occurrence of that same DP, establishing its own theme argument. Parallel Merge is represented through distinct occurrence identifiers with shared lineage, not through a multiply parented tree node. The two complement occurrences therefore identify one shared object, not two houses that merely happen to have matching descriptions. Neither occurrence has yet been assigned the final object pronunciation.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the shared DP in both verbal complement positions.

derivationStages.stageRecord: An unpronounced transitive v merges with each VP. Mary then merges as the external argument of the buying predicate, and John as the external argument of the selling predicate. These positions establish the respective agent roles. The same local transitive configurations license accusative on the two object occurrences. These are separate syntactic licensing dependencies even though the object occurrences share one DP identity.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce the external arguments and transitive little-v domains.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Each object occurrence internally merges at the right edge of its own vP, leaving a silent complement copy. These intermediate positions are necessary under the adopted phasal treatment of transitive v: subsequent right-node raising must access an edge occurrence rather than extract directly from a transferred VP. Rightward ordering is a linearization commitment of this right-node-raising analysis; the syntactic operation remains binary Internal Merge. The two edge occurrences retain their shared DP identity. They are accessible but have not yet received a surface token assignment.
derivationStages.statement: Move the shared object's occurrences to the two vP edges.

values.morphologicalCommitment: The lexical verb is represented as the whole word bought.
The lexical verb is represented as the whole word sold.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent past-tense T merges above each vP. The first T agrees with Mary and licenses nominative; the second agrees with John and licenses nominative. The object occurrences already have accusative and do not intervene as active Case goals. Each T also licenses the corresponding finite past verb. Bought and sold are retained as whole-word verbal terminals: this analysis does not decompose their irregular morphology or posit an overt auxiliary. Subject raising has not yet occurred, so both subjects remain in their previously established external-argument positions.
derivationStages.statement: Establish finite tense and subject licensing in both conjuncts.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Mary internally merges at the left edge of the first TP to satisfy its T's subject-position requirement. John then undergoes the corresponding operation in the second TP. Their higher occurrences carry the name pronunciations, and their original external-argument occurrences become silent copies. Both source positions were present before this stage. The object edge occurrences remain unchanged and accessible for the later across-the-board operation.
derivationStages.statement: Raise Mary and John to their respective finite subject positions.

values.interpretation: conjunction of the buying and selling propositions

derivationStages.stageRecord: And first merges with the John clause, and the Mary clause then merges as the other conjunct. This binary structure coordinates TPs, not merely verbs or VPs: the two overt subjects and independently licensed finite predicates belong to separate clauses. The first clause asserts a buying event and the second a selling event, with the shared DP remaining accessible at both vP edges. Coordination itself does not impose a temporal order on those events. No intervening CP phase is projected in this analysis of the coordinated finite declaratives.
derivationStages.statement: Coordinate the two finite clauses while preserving both object dependencies.

values.coverage: Both conjuncts supply an object occurrence of the same DP.
values.pronunciation: Only the final shared DP occurrence is pronounced.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The shared DP internally merges once more, now at a right-adjoined position outside the completed coordination. This single higher occurrence continues both object chains: extraction is across the board because each conjunct contains the corresponding source occurrence. Both previously accessible vP-edge occurrences become silent, while the higher DP receives the pronunciation the house. The original VP-complement copies remain silent and retain the thematic and Case dependencies established earlier. The output therefore says that Mary bought the same house that John sold, without asserting who bought from whom or ordering the two events. The comma placement marks the right-node-raising contour; it is not analyzed as an additional lexical item or as evidence that the second clause is a parenthetical. The final pronounced yield is exactly Mary bought and John sold the house.
derivationStages.statement: Complete across-the-board right-node raising and pronounce the shared object once.

values.解释: 进食事件达到由“完”指定的终结点

derivationStages.stageRecord: 本读法同样把“吃完”分析为词汇性结果复合动词：“吃”提供进食活动，“完”提供该事件的终结点。复合动词向补足语“苹果”指派主题角色。“完”本身已经使谓词具有终结性，但终结性不等于句法上的完成体；这一点允许后续把“了”分析为句末状态变化标记，而不是完成体中心语。外部论元仍留待把字轻动词层引入，当前动词短语指定语为空。
derivationStages.statement: 建立结果复合谓词，暂不引入完成体中心语。

values.链类型: A链；高位项统制并约束低位语迹

values.理论承诺: 把管辖其VP补足语边缘；低位V不另行指派结构宾格

derivationStages.stageRecord: 先以“把”为轻动词中心语，将现有动词短语置于其补足语位置，并在把字短语指定语位置引入“张伟”。轻动词和词汇谓词共同向“张伟”指派施事角色，不增加另一个独立致使事件。随后把“苹果”从上一阶段的动词补足语位置移到动词短语指定语位置，留下不发音的语迹。该论元链由高位名词短语统制和约束低位语迹，主题角色仍在低位取得。采用的把字轻动词分析让“把”管辖其补足语边缘的指定语位置，并在那里许可宾格和受影响对象的解释；低位动词不另外向同一论元指派结构宾格。本阶段没有加入完成体层，这正是本读法与完成体读法的结构区别之一。
derivationStages.statement: 建立把字轻动词结构及宾语移位链。

values.链类型: A链；高位项统制并约束低位语迹

values.许可配置: 有限句屈折中心语与其指定语

values.条件: 两个指称表达式均不被另一个共指名词短语约束

values.解释: 张伟把苹果吃完这一情状现在成立或成为当前相关的新情状

derivationStages.stageRecord: 先在把字短语外建立具有不发音有限句中心语的屈折短语，再把“张伟”从上一阶段的把字短语指定语提升到屈折短语指定语，留下受高位主语统制和约束的语迹。有限句中心语向高位主语许可主格；低位施事角色与高位格位置构成同一个论元链。这里的有限性是抽象句法许可，不要求汉语出现可见的时态词尾。两个指称名词短语不构成违反约束原则C的共指关系。随后，在完整屈折短语之外建立中心语居后的补语标记短语，把“了”放在句末中心语位置，令它以整个命题为作用域，标示‘张伟把苹果吃完’这一情状现在成立或具有新的当前关联。结果谓词仍表达进食达到终点，但本读法不另设完成体“了”。因此，语义重心是新情状的成立，而非单纯把事件作为完整发生的事件呈现。句末“了”紧邻动词只是线性结果，不需要动词移位或形态融合。
derivationStages.statement: 完成主语提升，并把“了”分析为句末状态变化中心语。

derivationStages.stageRecord: Select the relational noun adik, meaning younger sibling, and the third-person enclitic pronoun -nya. On this reading, -nya supplies the possessor argument of the kinship noun. Its referent remains open: it can be Ali or another contextually salient individual. Those reference choices do not require different syntactic structures. The two items are initially separate workspace objects; their joint written realization has not yet been established.
derivationStages.statement: Select the material for a possessive interpretation of adiknya.

values.interpretation: younger sibling of the third-person referent

derivationStages.stageRecord: Externally merge the pronominal possessor as the complement of relational adik, establishing the younger-sibling relation between the noun and the pronoun's referent. Merge a silent referential D above the resulting nominal. The pronounced order is noun followed by possessor. Establish enclitic realization of these two terminals as the single written word adiknya; their lexical forms remain unchanged. Labels identify the selecting head throughout, rather than introducing X-bar projection levels.
derivationStages.statement: Build the possessed nominal adiknya.

values.interpretation: the book is intended for the younger sibling

values.licensing: inherent theme licensing without an overt Case exponent

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a silent low applicative head with bare buku, then merge the possessed nominal in its specifier. The applicative relates the younger sibling to the book as its intended recipient or prospective possessor; it does not assert that possession was successfully transferred. Buku is a number-neutral bare nominal, so this structure does not impose an English singular indefinite determiner. In the Case implementation adopted here, the applicative licenses its theme internally, leaving the higher recipient nominal available for structural object licensing. The resulting recipient-before-theme order is the order required by this double-object use of membelikan.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the recipient–theme applicative domain.

values.morphologicalCommitment: whole-word exponent with active and benefactive-applicative features

values.licensing: structural object Case without an overt Case exponent

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the lexical verb membelikan with the applicative domain, and then merge active agentive v. This analysis selects membelikan as a whole-word verbal exponent: its lexical specification combines buying, the active meN- morphology, and the benefactive applicative -kan morphology. Accordingly, the silent functional heads are licensed by the features of this verb; the analysis does not posit separate pronounced affix terminals or covert head movement. Once active v is present, it licenses the higher internal nominal adiknya as the structural object, while buku retains its applicative-internal licensing. Finally, externally merge Ali at the edge of v, establishing the agent relation. This lower subject occurrence is pronounced at this stage and is the only available source for subsequent subject movement.
derivationStages.statement: Build the active buying predicate and introduce Ali as agent.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge silent finite T with the completed v-domain. T probes the accessible subject Ali in its already established external-argument position and licenses its abstract nominative Case. There is no overt agreement or tense exponent, and the sentence itself does not force a past, present, or future interpretation. The analysis adopts a subject-edge requirement on T, but movement has not yet applied: this workspace explicitly preserves the lower subject position from which the next operation will proceed.
derivationStages.statement: Merge finite T and license the lower subject.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge Ali from the previously represented v-edge to the edge of T, satisfying T's subject-edge requirement. The new upper occurrence and the retained lower occurrence form one movement chain. Pronounce the upper copy and silence the lower copy; the lower occurrence retains its lexical content and thematic position. The resulting order is Ali, membelikan, adiknya, buku. The completed root is a finite declarative T-object; no independently motivated complementizer is added. On this analysis, the sentence says that Ali buys or bought a book or books for someone's younger sibling, with the possessor's reference and the event's temporal location supplied by context.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the clause by raising Ali to the T-edge.

cases.description: Stage 7 elides b_vP with a neutral rewrite. The coordinator and the coordination that joins both clauses were unanchored construction and appeared only at the Stage Record (frame 51). They now have their own steps.

cases.sentence: John will eat beans, and Mary will rice.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Externally merge eat with beans. The bare plural beans is a maximal nominal without a projected silent determiner, and eat assigns it the Theme role. Projection labels identify the projecting head; they do not introduce an X-bar template. This analysis takes the final rice to be a nominal remnant of auxiliary-stranding ellipsis.
derivationStages.statement: Build the first clause's lexical predicate.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a silent transitive v with the existing predicate, then externally merge John at its edge. The proper name is represented as a maximal D. The external-argument relation connects John to the event introduced by v, and transitive v values the nominal object's accusative Case.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce John as the first clause's external argument.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge finite modal T, pronounced will, above the existing vP. T agrees with John in its previously established argument position and values nominative Case. Internal Merge then places a second occurrence of John at the T edge, satisfying T's subject requirement. The higher occurrence is pronounced and the lower occurrence is silenced. Eat remains in V; no overt verb movement is needed with the modal.
derivationStages.statement: Build the first finite clause and raise John.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Independently merge a second eat with the mass nominal rice, establishing their predicate–Theme relation. Merge silent transitive v and then Mary as its external argument. This establishes Mary's Agent role and rice's accusative Case. The second eat is still pronounced at this stage: its later silence will result from ellipsis, not from an initially empty lexical predicate.
derivationStages.statement: Build the second clause's underlying eat-rice predicate.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a silent contrastive head F above the second vP. F bears the ellipsis feature and attracts the object already present inside that vP. Internal Merge places rice at the F edge, outside the prospective deletion domain. The higher object occurrence is pronounced and the lower occurrence is silenced. This is the remnant movement required by the chosen pseudogapping analysis; it is not deletion of an isolated verb in situ.
derivationStages.statement: Evacuate rice from the prospective ellipsis domain.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the second finite will above FP. T agrees with Mary in her existing vP position and values nominative Case, then internally merges Mary at its edge. Rice does not intervene in this A-dependency: it is an already Case-valued nominal at a contrastive edge. Pronounce the higher Mary occurrence and silence the lower one. The resulting order places will before the evacuated object, while eat remains inside the still undeleted vP.
derivationStages.statement: Build the second finite clause and raise Mary.

values.identityCondition: identity after abstraction over contrasting subject and object alternatives

values.operation: PF nonpronunciation of the vP complement of F

derivationStages.stageRecord: Establish contrastive parallelism between John and Mary and between beans and rice. Abstracting over those contrasting arguments supplies the shared background eat(x,y), licensing the first vP as antecedent for the second. With the overt modal providing the auxiliary environment, F's ellipsis feature suppresses its vP complement, including the second eat; the evacuated rice and raised Mary remain outside that domain. This commits to focus-sensitive ellipsis identity rather than literal identity of the two vPs. Finally merge and with the second TP and merge the first TP as the other conjunct. The completed interpretation is that John will eat beans and Mary will eat rice. Auxiliary-stranding pseudogapping has speaker- and discourse-sensitive acceptability; this structure represents the elliptical reading where it is licensed.
derivationStages.statement: License auxiliary-stranding ellipsis and complete the coordination.
